option_description: Whether logs from all logging-capable assets are forwarded into one central SIEM/data lake, establishing the correlation substrate so no single source is the only copy.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "Centralized multi-source log aggregation" — fires when centralized_log_aggregation is true — providing the cross-source substrate (CIS 8.9 / AU-6(3)) without which multi-step attacks (T1078, T1021) are never linkable. Without it, each source sits in a siloed console and an attacker who clears one source's local log erases the only copy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the source-onboarding inventory and confirm each in-scope asset class forwards to the central SIEM, meeting CIS 8.9 centralization and 8.2 collection across logging-capable assets.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Source-onboarding inventory shows each asset class forwarding to the central SIEM (secure) vs. gaps where a class is unmonitored (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (Audit Log Management)

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the SIEM, enumerate active source types and their last-seen timestamps to confirm live multi-source forwarding into the central platform.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM > Data Inputs / Source Types — enumerate active source types and last-seen timestamps per source class
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Recent events from every in-scope source class (secure) vs. stale/absent feeds (silent blind spot)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (Audit Log Management)

option_description: Whether every in-scope logging-capable asset class (host/EDR, network, identity/IdP, cloud, application) is actively forwarding with fresh last-seen timestamps — no silent blind-spot class.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Centralized multi-source log aggregation" — fires when required_log_source_classes_onboarded is true. An un-onboarded class (e.g. identity or cloud) is a blind spot through which a multi-step chain (T1078) escapes; the protection is present only when all in-scope classes report fresh ingest.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM > Data Inputs / Source Types, enumerate active source types and last-seen timestamps per source class; compare the onboarded set against the in-scope asset inventory and confirm each class shows recent (non-stale) ingest.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM > Data Inputs / Source Types — enumerate active source types and last-seen timestamps per source class
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Recent events from every in-scope source class (secure) vs. stale/absent feeds for a class (silent blind spot)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (Audit Log Management)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check the SIEM source-class set against the authoritative asset inventory to verify no in-scope class (host/EDR, network, identity, cloud, application) is missing.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every in-scope asset class appears in the onboarding inventory with live forwarding (secure) vs. a class present in the asset inventory but absent from ingest (gap)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (Audit Log Management)

option_description: Whether the aggregated correlation substrate is stored on infrastructure isolated from the monitored assets, so a source's identity cannot delete its own forwarded records.
security_impact: Contextual evidence for "Centralized multi-source log aggregation" and load-bearing in the retention/tamper facet. When false, an attacker who compromises a source (T1070) can erase its own copy of the multi-step trail; separate-system storage satisfies AU-9(2).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the SIEM/log store runs on infrastructure isolated from the monitored sources and that source identities cannot delete forwarded records, satisfying AU-9(2) separate-system storage.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AU-9(2) separate-system storage satisfied — logs on isolated infrastructure, source identities unable to alter/delete (secure) vs. mutable co-located logs (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU family — AU-9 Protection of Audit Information

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the network/hosting topology of the SIEM to verify it is administratively and network-segregated from the asset population whose logs it stores.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SIEM deployed in a separate management/security zone with restricted inbound write-only forwarding (secure) vs. log store reachable and deletable from monitored assets (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether enabled correlation rules stitch events across multiple repositories/source classes (identity, host/EDR, network, cloud) rather than evaluating each source in isolation.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Cross-source multi-stage correlation into a single incident" — fires when cross_source_correlation_enabled is true — satisfying AU-6(3) cross-repository correlation. Without it a multi-step chain spanning sources (T1078/T1021/T1071) is never linked.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the documented correlation searches and confirm at least some join >=2 source repositories, satisfying AU-6(3) 'analyze and correlate audit records across different repositories'.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented correlation searches that join >=2 source repositories (secure) vs. only single-source rules (the gap)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-6(3) Correlate Audit Record Repositories

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM > Correlation Searches / Analytic Rules, filter to enabled multi-datamodel rules and confirm rules draw from more than one source type.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM > Correlation Searches / Analytic Rules — filter to enabled multi-datamodel rules
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enabled rules drawing from multiple source types (secure) vs. single-source, single-event rules only (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-6(5) Integrated Analysis of Audit Records

option_description: Whether at least one enabled multi-datamodel correlation rule exists per major attack chain (lateral movement, C2, credential access) that links sequential stages into a single incident object.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Cross-source multi-stage correlation into a single incident" — fires when multistage_incident_correlation_enabled is true. It is the core protection of this control: linking sequential stages (IdP brute-force -> host EDR alert -> lateral movement) into one incident surfaces chains (T1021/T1110) invisible to any single-source rule.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM > Correlation Searches / Analytic Rules, confirm there is at least one enabled rule per major attack chain (lateral movement, C2, credential access) that links sequential stages into one incident/notable object.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM > Correlation Searches / Analytic Rules — filter to enabled multi-datamodel rules
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one enabled rule per major attack chain drawing from multiple source types and producing a single incident (secure) vs. isolated per-stage alerts (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-6(5) Integrated Analysis of Audit Records

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify by walking one chain end-to-end (e.g. IdP brute-force then host EDR alert then lateral movement) that the searches emit a single incident object rather than separate alerts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Sequential stages collapse into one incident/notable (secure) vs. each stage emitting an isolated, unlinked alert (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-6(3) Correlate Audit Record Repositories

option_description: Whether every enabled detection/correlation rule is tagged with one or more MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs, so coverage can be quantified per technique rather than assumed.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "ATT&CK-mapped detection coverage with gap measurement" — fires when detection_rules_attack_mapped is true. Without per-rule technique tags, coverage cannot be measured and undetected techniques stay invisible (enterprise SIEMs miss ~79% of techniques when coverage is unmeasured).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Sample enabled detection rules and confirm each carries one or more ATT&CK technique IDs; verify against the ATT&CK Navigator-style coverage heatmap that mappings exist and untagged rules are the exception.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ATT&CK Navigator-style coverage heatmap exists and each detection maps to technique IDs (secure) vs. rules untagged / no coverage map (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: ReliaQuest — Measuring Detection Coverage with MITRE ATT&CK

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the SIEM rule editor, inspect the technique/annotation field of a representative sample of enabled correlation rules to confirm ATT&CK IDs are populated.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM > Correlation Searches / Analytic Rules > (rule) > Annotations / MITRE ATT&CK mapping
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Technique IDs populated on enabled rules (secure) vs. blank ATT&CK annotation fields (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: ReliaQuest — Measuring Detection Coverage with MITRE ATT&CK

option_description: Whether an ATT&CK Navigator-style coverage heatmap is maintained and trended over time, with zero-coverage techniques tracked to closure.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "ATT&CK-mapped detection coverage with gap measurement" — fires when attack_coverage_measured_and_trended is true. Turns detection from assumed to quantified; without trending and a tracked gap backlog, blind spots persist undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the coverage heatmap/dashboard for a periodic trend line (e.g. Q1 45% -> Q3 68%) and a tracked backlog of zero-coverage techniques driven to closure.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Coverage metric computed against the ATT&CK matrix with a trend line and a gap backlog (secure); coverage never measured / gaps unknown (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Help Net Security — Enterprise SIEMs miss 79% of known MITRE ATT&CK techniques

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the coverage assessment follows a repeatable methodology (inventory data sources, iterate each technique, map alerts, classify covered/partial/zero) so the trend is comparable period over period.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented, repeated coverage-measurement method producing comparable period figures (secure) vs. one-off or ad-hoc estimate (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: ReliaQuest — Measuring Detection Coverage with MITRE ATT&CK

option_description: Percentage of in-scope MITRE ATT&CK techniques that have at least one TESTED detection. Read it from the coverage dashboard; the protection is effective at >= 80%.
security_impact: One of the conditions of "ATT&CK-mapped detection coverage with gap measurement" — the protection is present when attack_technique_coverage_pct >= 80. Below threshold, a meaningful fraction of techniques (e.g. T1071/T1098/T1003) have no tested detection — the documented baseline is ~79% of techniques missed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the measured coverage figure from the ATT&CK heatmap/dashboard and confirm it counts only techniques with a TESTED (not merely authored) detection. The secure threshold is >= 80% of in-scope techniques covered.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A numeric coverage percentage, e.g. 82, computed against the in-scope ATT&CK matrix using tested detections; >= 80 is secure, lower indicates a coverage shortfall
how_to_obtain.source: ReliaQuest — Measuring Detection Coverage with MITRE ATT&CK

how_to_obtain.instruction: Spot-check that the percentage denominator is the in-scope technique set and that 'tested' means validation/detonation evidence exists, not just an authored rule, so the figure is not inflated.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Coverage % traces to a defined in-scope denominator and tested-detection numerator (secure) vs. authored-but-untested rules counted as covered (overstated)
how_to_obtain.source: Help Net Security — Enterprise SIEMs miss 79% of known MITRE ATT&CK techniques

option_description: Whether User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) is enabled, modeling normal user/entity activity and scoring deviations to catch novel and credential-abuse attacks that static signatures miss.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Behavioral and UEBA anomaly analytics" — fires when ueba_anomaly_analytics_enabled is true — providing D3FEND D3-UBA behavioral detection mitigating valid-account abuse and credential access (T1078/T1110/T1003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM/UEBA > Models / Anomaly Rules, confirm a behavioral analytics module is active and producing anomaly scores against live telemetry (mapping to D3FEND D3-UBA).
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM/UEBA > Models / Anomaly Rules — confirm baselining is trained and anomaly detectors active
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active behavioral models scoring live telemetry, mapping to D3FEND D3-UBA (secure); static signature rules only, no behavioral layer (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE D3FEND — User Behavior Analysis (D3-UBA)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the UEBA module is licensed/enabled in production (not a disabled trial) and that its anomaly scores feed downstream correlation/risk scoring rather than sitting in a separate dead-end console.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: UEBA enabled and integrated into the alerting pipeline (secure) vs. present but disabled / disconnected (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Exabeam — UEBA primer (risk-based alerting / false-positive reduction)

option_description: Whether per-user and per-entity behavioral baselines are trained and active, giving the analytics a learned reference rather than a cold/empty model.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Behavioral and UEBA anomaly analytics" — fires when entity_baseline_trained is true. A cold-start model produces noise or silence; a trained baseline is what lets anomaly scoring (D3-UBA) reliably flag deviation for credential-abuse detection (T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM/UEBA > Models, confirm baselines are trained and active (not cold-start) and that entities have established normal profiles before anomaly scoring is relied upon.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM/UEBA > Models / Anomaly Rules — confirm baselining is trained and anomaly detectors active
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Models report a trained/established baseline state with populated per-entity profiles (secure) vs. 'learning'/cold-start or empty profiles (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE D3FEND — User Behavior Analysis (D3-UBA)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the baseline has actually completed its initial training window for the in-scope entity population, not just for a pilot subset.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Baselines trained across the in-scope user/entity set (secure) vs. trained only for a pilot group leaving most entities cold (partial)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Length in days of the activity window over which the behavioral baseline is trained. Read the configured learning-window value; a window >= 14 days is required for a statistically meaningful profile.
security_impact: One of the conditions of "Behavioral and UEBA anomaly analytics" — the protection is present when baseline_training_window_days >= 14. Too short a window overfits to a brief sample, producing false anomalies or missing real deviation (D3-UBA reliability).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM/UEBA > Models, read the configured baseline training/learning window length and confirm it is at least 14 days. Research guidance notes a >30-day window as a strong baseline.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM/UEBA > Models / Anomaly Rules — confirm baselining is trained (>30-day window) and anomaly detectors active
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A configured window value in days (e.g. 30); >= 14 is the minimum secure threshold, with >30 preferred
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE D3FEND — User Behavior Analysis (D3-UBA)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the configured window reflects elapsed learning time on live data, not merely a setting that was just enabled with no history accumulated yet.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Window set to >= 14 days AND that much live history has accrued (secure) vs. long window configured but only days of data collected (effectively cold)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether geolocation-based impossible-travel logon detection is enabled — successive authentications from geographically distant locations within a physically impossible interval are flagged (D3FEND D3-UGLPA).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Behavioral and UEBA anomaly analytics" — fires when impossible_travel_detection_enabled is true — providing D3FEND D3-UGLPA geolocation-velocity analysis, surfacing valid-account abuse and credential theft (T1078/T1110).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM/UEBA > Models / Anomaly Rules, confirm a geolocation-velocity / impossible-travel detector is enabled against authentication events (maps to D3FEND D3-UGLPA).
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM/UEBA > Models / Anomaly Rules — confirm baselining is trained and anomaly detectors active
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An enabled impossible-travel / geo-velocity rule mapping to D3-UGLPA (secure) vs. no geolocation logon analysis (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE D3FEND — User Behavior Analysis (D3-UBA)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the detector receives authentication events enriched with source geolocation and that its alerts route into the notable/incident pipeline.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Geo-enriched authn events feeding an active impossible-travel detector wired to alerting (secure) vs. rule present but unfed or disconnected (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether authentication-event thresholding/anomaly analysis is enabled — abnormal volumes or patterns of authentication events (failed-logon spikes, off-baseline access) are detected (D3FEND D3-ANET).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Behavioral and UEBA anomaly analytics" — fires when authentication_thresholding_enabled is true — providing D3FEND D3-ANET authentication-event thresholding, catching brute-force and credential-reuse (T1110/T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM/UEBA > Models / Anomaly Rules, verify detection logic exists for abnormal authentication volumes/patterns (failed-logon spikes, off-baseline access), mapping to D3FEND D3-ANET.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM/UEBA > Models / Anomaly Rules — confirm baselining is trained and anomaly detectors active
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An enabled authentication-thresholding detector mapping to D3-ANET (secure) vs. no authn anomaly analysis (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE D3FEND — User Behavior Analysis (D3-UBA)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm thresholds are derived from the trained baseline (adaptive) rather than a single static count, so the detector tracks normal authentication volume per entity.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Baseline-driven adaptive thresholds (secure) vs. one fixed global threshold or none (weaker/insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Exabeam — UEBA primer (risk-based alerting / false-positive reduction)

option_description: Whether correlation/detection content (e.g. Sigma rules) is authored and maintained in version control rather than hand-edited in the SIEM console, giving change history, auditability, and rollback (CM-2/CM-3).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Detection-as-code rule lifecycle and content currency" — fires when detection_as_code_version_controlled is true — satisfying CM-2 version-controlled baseline. Hand-edited console rules have no audit trail or rollback, so a bad or removed rule silently loses coverage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm detection content lives in a VCS repository with commit history and that production rules are deployed FROM it rather than hand-edited in-console, satisfying CM-2.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A detection-as-code repo with commit history that is the deployment source of truth (secure) vs. ad-hoc console edits (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Configuration Management (CM) family

how_to_obtain.instruction: Validate the rule repository with sigma-cli to confirm rules are real version-controlled Sigma content that converts cleanly to the target backend.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: sigma-cli validates rule syntax and converts to the target SIEM query language with no errors (secure pipeline gate); validation errors indicate untested rules
how_to_obtain.source: SigmaHQ — Getting Started (sigma-cli)

option_description: Whether changes to detection content are merged only through peer-reviewed pull requests with required reviewer approval, enforcing the change-control gate (CM-3).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Detection-as-code rule lifecycle and content currency" — fires when detection_content_peer_reviewed is true — satisfying CM-3 change-control. Without a review gate, an unreviewed or malicious rule change reaches production unchecked.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the branch-protection / merge policy on the detection-content repo for a required-reviewer approval gate (CM-3 change control with security-impact analysis).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CM-3 change-control with required-reviewer approval satisfied (secure) vs. direct pushes to the production branch allowed (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Configuration Management (CM) family

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the repo host (e.g. GitHub/GitLab) settings, confirm the protected branch requires at least one approving review and blocks self-merge.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Repo > Settings > Branches / Branch protection — require pull request reviews before merging
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Required-approvals >= 1 with the production branch protected (secure) vs. no required reviews (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether detection content passes automated CI/CD testing — syntax validation, unit tests, and integration tests against sample telemetry — before deployment.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Detection-as-code rule lifecycle and content currency" — fires when detection_content_ci_tested is true. CI testing catches broken or non-firing rules pre-release; without it a syntactically valid but non-matching rule silently loses coverage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the CI pipeline runs syntax/unit/integration tests on detection content and gates deployment on those tests passing (the CM change-control test stage).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A detection-as-code repo with a CI test stage that gates deployment (secure) vs. rules deployed with no automated testing (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Configuration Management (CM) family

how_to_obtain.instruction: Reproduce the CI gate locally: run sigma check for syntax and sigma convert to confirm rules build against the target backend, mirroring the pipeline's pass condition.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: sigma-cli validates and converts with no errors (matches the CI pass condition); errors reveal rules that would fail or never fire
how_to_obtain.source: SigmaHQ — Getting Started (sigma-cli)

option_description: Maximum days between scheduled refreshes of detection content against evolving TTPs (vendor packs, community Sigma, new CVEs). Read the scheduled refresh interval; the protection is present at a cadence <= 90 days.
security_impact: One of the conditions of "Detection-as-code rule lifecycle and content currency" — the protection is present when detection_content_update_cadence_days <= 90. Stale, frozen rules silently lose coverage as attackers shift TTPs; a long cadence means new techniques (T1071/T1098) go undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine the scheduled refresh interval for detection content (vendor content packs / community Sigma) and confirm it is no greater than 90 days. Compare the applied content-pack/ruleset version against the latest available.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented update cadence in days and the latest content-pack/Sigma-ruleset version applied (secure at <= 90); last update months/years old (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-92 Guide to Computer Security Log Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the detection-content repo or CI schedule, confirm an automated/recurring job pulls upstream content within the stated cadence rather than relying on ad-hoc manual refreshes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A scheduled refresh job with commit/run history at or under the cadence (secure) vs. no recurring update mechanism (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether all log-producing sources synchronize their clocks to at least two approved/trusted NTP sources, so emitted timestamps share a common, drift-bounded reference.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Synchronized time for reliable event sequencing" — fires when clocks_synced_to_trusted_time_source is true — satisfying CIS 8.4 (>=2 synced sources) and AU-8. When false, clock drift mis-orders an attack chain's events and makes cross-source correlation (T1021/T1078) unreliable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm log sources sync to >= 2 approved/trusted NTP servers with bounded fleet-wide drift, satisfying CIS 8.4 'standardize time synchronization using at least two synchronized time sources' and AU-8.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 8.4 two-source time synchronization and AU-8 timestamp requirements met (secure) vs. clock drift / single or no NTP source (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (Audit Log Management)

how_to_obtain.instruction: On a representative log source, check the clock-sync state and configured NTP sources. (Linux: timedatectl status or chronyc tracking / chronyc sources; Windows: w32tm /query /status.)
how_to_obtain.command: timedatectl status   # or: chronyc tracking / w32tm /query /status
how_to_obtain.expected_output: System clock synchronized: yes, with >= 2 configured NTP sources (secure) vs. 'not synchronized' (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (Audit Log Management)

option_description: Whether ingested event timestamps from every source are normalized to a single canonical timezone (UTC) at ingest, eliminating mixed-timezone skew.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Synchronized time for reliable event sequencing" — fires when timestamps_in_utc is true. Mixed local timezones reaching correlation cause non-deterministic event ordering, breaking multi-stage chain reconstruction (T1021) even when clocks are synced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the ingest pipeline normalizes all event timestamps to UTC at ingest, with no mixed-local-timezone records reaching correlation (supports AU-8 timestamp consistency).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Ingest pipeline normalizes timestamps to UTC; no mixed-timezone records (secure) vs. mixed local timezones causing mis-ordering (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (Audit Log Management)

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the SIEM, inspect indexed event time fields across several source types and confirm the canonical/_time field is stored and displayed in UTC regardless of source locale.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM > search a sample across source types — inspect the canonical event-time field / timezone metadata
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Canonical event-time stored in UTC across all source types (secure) vs. per-source local-time values (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether events and entities are enriched at ingest/correlation time with threat intelligence (known-bad IP/domain/file-hash indicators) and asset/identity context.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Risk-based alerting with threat-intel enrichment" — fires when threat_intel_enrichment_enabled is true — satisfying AU-6(5) integrated analysis. Without enrichment, known-bad observables and asset criticality never feed the scoring layer, so chains (T1071) are scored blind.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM > Threat Intelligence / Enrichment, confirm active intel feeds and enrichment lookups are bound to correlation searches so known-bad indicators and asset/identity context join events at ingest/search time.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM > Threat Intelligence / Enrichment — confirm active intel feeds and enrichment lookups bound to correlation searches
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AU-6(5) integrated analysis with external intel satisfied; matches generate/raise notables (secure) vs. raw events with no enrichment (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-6(5) Integrated Analysis of Audit Records

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the threat-intel feeds are current (recent update timestamps) and that enrichment runs at ingest/correlation rather than being evaluated rule-by-rule in isolation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Live, recently-updated feeds joined at ingest/correlation (secure) vs. stale feeds or per-rule isolated lookups (weaker/insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-6(5) Integrated Analysis of Audit Records

option_description: Whether the platform assigns risk scores to enriched events/entities and raises an investigative notable only when accumulated risk crosses a threshold, instead of one alert per rule firing.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Risk-based alerting with threat-intel enrichment" — fires when risk_based_alerting_enabled is true — satisfying AU-6(5). Risk aggregation surfaces multi-step chains as a single prioritized notable; one-alert-per-rule buries the chain in fatigue.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In SIEM > Risk Analysis / Notable Event aggregation, confirm risk modifiers are attached to rules and that a risk-incident threshold governs when a notable fires (per-rule firing suppressed in favor of risk objects).
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM > Risk Analysis / Notable Event aggregation — confirm risk modifiers attached to rules and a risk-incident threshold
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Risk-based notables aggregate multiple contributing detections per entity above a threshold (secure) vs. raw per-rule alerts (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Exabeam — UEBA primer (risk-based alerting / false-positive reduction)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify risk scores accumulate per entity over a window and that the notable threshold is documented and tuned, confirming chains are scored rather than each rule firing independently.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-entity accumulated risk with a documented notable threshold (secure) vs. no risk aggregation / one alert per rule (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Exabeam — UEBA primer (risk-based alerting / false-positive reduction)

option_description: Whether an ongoing alert/false-positive tuning process exists (threshold review, suppression of benign-true patterns, periodic precision review) so the alerting layer stays effective over time.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Risk-based alerting with threat-intel enrichment" — fires when alert_tuning_process_enabled is true — satisfying the CIS 8.11 log-review cadence. Without tuning, false-positive noise buries real correlated incidents and analysts stop trusting alerts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a recurring tuning cadence exists with documented threshold review, suppression governance, and precision metrics — the CIS 8.11 'review logs' loop with analyst feedback retraining models/thresholds.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 8.11 review cadence and a tuning record exist; FP rate tracked and trending down (secure) vs. rules deployed once and never tuned (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (Audit Log Management)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review tuning/suppression change records and confirm suppressions are governed (justified, reviewed, time-bounded) rather than blanket mutes that could hide real detections.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Governed, documented suppressions with justification and review (secure) vs. ad-hoc blanket mutes (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Exabeam — UEBA primer (risk-based alerting / false-positive reduction)

option_description: Whether surfaced notable incidents auto-route to the IR queue and are governed by a defined, enforced response-time SLA (IR-4/IR-5), reducing attacker dwell time.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Alerting SLA, SOAR handoff, and protected evidence retention" — fires when alert_response_sla_enforced is true — satisfying IR-4/IR-5. Detection without a time-bound response does not reduce dwell time; notables sit unactioned.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm notables are time-bound to an owner with a tracked response SLA and that breaches are measured, satisfying IR-4 incident handling and IR-5 incident monitoring with measured time-to-acknowledge.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IR-4/IR-5 satisfied: notables flow into the IR process with measured time-to-acknowledge against an SLA (secure) vs. orphaned alerts (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 IR-4 / IR-5 (Incident Handling and Monitoring)

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the IR/ticketing queue, review SLA configuration and recent notable tickets for response-time tracking and breach reporting.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IR/SOAR queue > SLA policy and ticket metrics — review response-time targets and breach reports
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Defined SLA targets with per-ticket response timers and breach metrics (secure) vs. no SLA / untracked tickets (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether correlated incidents auto-route into the SOAR / IR ticketing workflow (case creation, orchestration, playbook handoff) instead of remaining console-only alerts.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Alerting SLA, SOAR handoff, and protected evidence retention" — fires when soar_response_handoff_enabled is true — satisfying IR-4. It closes the detection-to-response loop; console-only alerts that no one watches leave detections unactioned.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify correlated notables automatically create cases/tickets in the SOAR or IR workflow rather than living only in the SIEM console, satisfying IR-4 incident handling.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IR-4 satisfied: notables flow into the IR/SOAR process automatically (secure) vs. alerts landing in a console no one watches (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 IR-4 / IR-5 (Incident Handling and Monitoring)

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the SOAR/SIEM integration settings, confirm an automated case-creation/playbook handoff is configured and review recent auto-created cases to prove the route is live.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM/SOAR > Response Actions / Integrations — confirm auto case creation and playbook handoff are enabled
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Recent SOAR/IR cases auto-created from notables via an enabled integration (secure) vs. no handoff configured (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether the centralized log/SIEM store is integrity-protected via write-once / cryptographic tamper-evidence and access-restricted (AU-9(2)/(3)/(4)).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of "Alerting SLA, SOAR handoff, and protected evidence retention" — fires when audit_log_tamper_evident is true — satisfying AU-9(3) cryptographic integrity and AU-9(4) restricted audit management. Without it, an attacker who reaches the SIEM can silently erase or alter the multi-step trail (T1070).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the log store uses write-once / cryptographic integrity protection and restricts who can alter or delete retained records, satisfying AU-9(2) separate-system, AU-9(3) cryptographic integrity, and AU-9(4) restricted audit management.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AU-9(2)/(3)/(4) satisfied — separate-system, integrity-protected, audit-management-restricted store (secure) vs. mutable, broadly accessible logs (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU family — AU-9 Protection of Audit Information

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the log-store / object-store settings, confirm WORM / immutability (e.g. retention lock) is enabled and review the access-control roles permitted to delete or modify retained data.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Log store / object store > Retention / Immutability settings and IAM roles — confirm WORM lock on and delete rights restricted
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Immutability/WORM enabled and delete/modify rights limited to a privileged subset (secure) vs. mutable store with broad delete rights (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Number of days correlated events are retained hot/online. Read the configured online/hot retention period; the protection is present at >= 90 days (CIS 8.10).
security_impact: One of the conditions of "Alerting SLA, SOAR handoff, and protected evidence retention" — the protection is present when log_retention_days >= 90 (CIS 8.10). Short retention means the early stages of a slow, multi-month campaign are gone before correlation/IR reaches them.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured online/hot retention period for correlated events and confirm it is at least 90 days, meeting CIS 8.10 'retain audit logs for a minimum of 90 days' with integrity-protected archival beyond that per SP 800-92.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A configured hot/searchable retention value in days; CIS 8.10 met at >= 90 (secure) vs. sub-week retention (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (Audit Log Management)

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the SIEM index/storage policy, read the searchable retention setting per index and confirm correlated-event indexes meet >= 90 days, with longer archival where regulation requires.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM > Indexes / Storage policy — read searchable retention period per relevant index
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Index retention >= 90 days for correlated-event data (secure) vs. logs rotated/expired in days (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge
